item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports testing separate representations of immediate intent and enduring preferences, but does not establish that a single SASRec representation necessarily conflates them. [HLSDMRec (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104425) combines a local LSTM for short-term transitions, denoised Mamba for long-term preferences, and adaptive fusion. [C-TLSAN (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13021) incorporates item descriptions into long- and short-term attention, reporting improvements across ten Amazon categories. [GLSRec (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.datak.2026.102606) additionally models transitions across users’ sequences, addressing the limited transition evidence within sparse individual histories. These results motivate architectural ablations; their reported gains cannot be transferred directly to the pinned RecHarness evaluation.\n\nA practical hypothesis for this benchmark: retain SASRec, add a recent-window intent branch and a pooled historical-preference branch, then learn a small gate conditioned on history length, representation agreement, and observed interaction gaps. Compare against fixed fusion and each branch alone. For temporal modeling, foundational [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) combines absolute positions with relative time intervals and evaluates Amazon CDs/Vinyl, among other datasets. Test a lightweight bucketed time-gap attention bias before adopting a larger encoder. Recurrent interests could be represented through similarity to previously observed items, while recommendations still exclude seen items. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated benchmark improvements. Select using the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; use only historical timestamps and permitted item text, with any text encoder trained locally."}
